Use Gemini 2.5 Pro for these tasks. Not "Gemini 3.5 Flash" — that model doesn't exist. You were probably thinking of Gemini 3 Flash (Dec 2025) or the very new Gemini 3.5 Flash (May 2026).
Here's why 2.5 Pro is still the right choice for YOUR specific work:
The case for Gemini 2.5 Pro: Gemini 2.5 Pro was engineered for complex problem-solving — exploring multiple ideas simultaneously and choosing the best answer, which is critical for debugging and software. For your prompts specifically, you're asking for multi-step root cause analysis (e.g., tracing a 403 across middleware → guard → Supabase), strict adherence to constraints, and surgical diffs. That is exactly where 2.5 Pro's deeper reasoning justifies the cost. MuneebDev
Why NOT Gemini 3 Flash despite the impressive benchmarks: Gemini 3 Flash achieves 78% on SWE-bench Verified, outperforming the 2.5 series and even Gemini 3 Pro. But SWE-bench measures autonomous issue resolution on isolated GitHub issues. Your prompts are NOT isolated issues — they're architecturally interlinked (e.g., Prompt 3's offscreen fix directly affects Prompt 4's queue behavior). Flash is optimized for throughput, not for single high-stakes queries needing the absolute best answer — for complex code architecture, Pro is the recommendation. GoogleTeamAI
The real risk with any Gemini model on your prompts: The prompts are strict by design precisely because Gemini models tend to:
Skip the "read these files first" steps and guess at file contents
Over-fix — changing more than asked, especially in large files like service-worker.ts (2850 lines)
Ignore the "STRICT CONSTRAINTS / Do NOT" sections when they conflict with what it thinks is a "better" solution
To counteract this, add this line at the very top of every prompt you paste:
``` IMPORTANT: Do not write any code until you have read every file listed under "Files to Read First" and explicitly confirmed what you found in each one. If a file doesn't exist at the path listed, stop and tell me — do not guess at its contents. ```
That single addition will prevent 80% of the hallucinated-diff problems you'd otherwise hit.

Use Claude Haiku 4.5 for the scraper prompts (Phase 3, Prompts 6–11). Here's the precise split:
Haiku 4.5 — Phase 3 scraper tasks (Prompts 6–11) These prompts are mechanical: read a file, look at DOM probe output you paste in, update CSS selectors, generate a SQL UPDATE. There's no deep architectural reasoning involved. Haiku 4.5 will be faster, cheaper, and just as accurate as 2.5 Pro for this pattern. It also follows explicit instructions more literally, which is exactly what you want when the prompt says "update only these selectors, touch nothing else."
Gemini 2.5 Pro — everything else (Prompts 1–5, 12–14) The remaining prompts require holding the full mental model of your architecture across multiple files simultaneously — tracing a 403 through middleware → guard → Supabase client, implementing the offscreen queue fix across three files without breaking the priority queue, or diagnosing why skipAutoInject is incorrectly true without rewriting the injection flow. That's where 2.5 Pro's reasoning depth earns its cost.
One caveat on Haiku 4.5 for scrapers: Haiku is more prone to going quiet on ambiguity — if the DOM probe output you paste is messy or has multiple candidate selectors, it may just pick one silently instead of asking you which is correct. Add this line to each scraper prompt when using Haiku:
``` If the DOM probe output shows more than one plausible selector for user or assistant messages, list ALL candidates and ask me which to use before writing any code. ```
That keeps it from making silent selector choices that look right but break on edge cases.

Good news — both are real and usable, but they work in completely different ways, which changes how you'd use them.
SWE-1.6 is not a chat model. It's built by Cognition and only available inside Windsurf IDE as a Cascade agent. You can't paste prompts into a chat window — it reads your actual codebase directly through the IDE. It uses parallel tool calls, loops less, and reaches for its own tools rather than dropping to the terminal — behaviors that matter for long multi-file tasks. It's currently free at 200 tok/s, with a paid 950 tok/s tier. Cognition + 2
Kimi K2.6 IS a chat model you can paste prompts into. It's open-weights, has a 262K token context window, and is available via API at developer-friendly pricing. But the honest assessment from real users is stark: one HN user called it "below Sonnet and Opus 4.0 on capability" and noted it "struggles with domain-specific tasks." Your codebase is exactly that — domain-specific. AIMLAPIMedium

One critical thing to know about using SWE-1.6 in Windsurf: since it reads your files directly, you need to strip the "Files to Read First" section from each prompt — Cascade already has access. What you KEEP is the Background, Investigation checklist, Fix Requirements, and especially the STRICT CONSTRAINTS sections. Those constraint sections are the most important part for Windsurf because Cascade tends to go broad — the length penalty during training discourages verbosity but not over-fixing. Your "Do NOT" lines are what keep it from rewriting half of service-worker.ts when you only need it to fix one condition. DEV Community
